correctness.rationale: Direct commutator multiplication gives three alternating matrix identities; the solution set splits exhaustively into affine X, proportional-column Y, and Lagrangian isotropic Z. Y is a constant-rank vector-bundle closure of dimension 3m+3; Z is the image of a rank-2m vector bundle over LG(2,4), yielding dimension 3m+3 for m>=2; X has dimension 4m. Closed rank-three witnesses separate all three for m>=3. A direct algebraic one-parameter specialization proves X lies in Y when m=2. Char-2 compatibility is explicit. Independent finite-field enumerations in verify.py check nine small configurations and the full central coordinate for one case. Reduced vs scheme-theoretic statements are distinguished.

value.rationale: The component count/dimension/equidimensionality is a natural algebro-geometric invariant of the commuting-tuple scheme of a classical six-dimensional nilradical. A complete geometric classification across unbounded m and all characteristics, with the sharp transition from two components for pairs to three for triples and failure of equidimensionality at quadruples, is structurally motivated and not a routine finite computation. The symplectic incidence construction explains the extra component. Finite-field count alone would not justify value.
